title: Active recall strategies associated with academic achievement in young adults: A  systematic review.
authors: Xu, Joy | Wu, Alyssa | Filip, Cosmina | Patel, Zinal | Bernstein, Sarah R | Tanveer, Rameen | Syed, Hiba | Kotroczo, Tiffany
access_status: publisher abstract and bibliographic record; full text not openly retrieved
corpus_or_sample: number of included studies not reported in the accessible abstract
mechanism_or_intervention: flashcards; practice testing/retrieval practice; concept mapping
principal_findings: Flashcard use was popular and correlated with higher grades/test scores; self-testing, retrieval practice and concept mapping were described as promising but underused; concept mapping was associated with confidence.
quantitative_summary: No pooled effect; qualitative synthesis in accessible abstract.
key_limitations: Heterogeneous studies; accessible abstract does not provide included-study table or sufficient detail to separate association from causal effects; corrigendum exists.
next_action: Request or obtain full text before using included-study counts or quality judgments.

title: Quantifying cognitive and affective impacts of Quizlet on learning outcomes: a  systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.
corpus_or_sample: 23 included studies; 21 effects for achievement, 5 for retention, 2 for attitude
comparison: traditional instruction, alternative study conditions or control groups across included studies
principal_findings: Moderate average effects were reported for vocabulary achievement and retention and a small positive effect for attitude.
quantitative_summary: Achievement g=0.628, 95% CI 0.370–0.885, I²=82.3%; retention g=0.743, 95% CI 0.241–1.245, I²=80.9%; attitude fixed-effect g=0.377, 95% CI 0.029–0.725, based on 2 studies.
key_limitations: High heterogeneity for achievement and retention; only two attitude studies; product features and instructional contexts varied; longitudinal and informal/self-directed evidence was limited.
next_action: Retain as central product meta-analysis; map its primary studies against the 2025 Quizlet review to avoid double counting.

title: Systematic review of distributed practice and retrieval practice in health  professions education.
authors: Trumble, Emma | Lodge, Jason | Mandrusiak, Allison | Forbes, Roma
journal: Advances in health sciences education : theory and practice
comparison: varied control and active comparison groups
outcomes: academic grades and examination scores; implementation variables
principal_findings: Most included experiments reported benefits of distributed or retrieval practice, but interventions, assessments and designs were heterogeneous.
quantitative_summary: 43 of 63 experiments reported statistically significant benefits; mean MERSQI 12.23/18 and NOS-E 4.55/6.
key_limitations: Heterogeneous interventions and outcomes; incomplete reporting of content, time on task, delays and assessment stakes; significance counts do not provide a pooled causal effect.
next_action: Retain as central applied review; map primary studies against radiology, nursing and medical spaced-repetition reviews.

title: A Scoping Review of Retrieval Practice (Test-Enhanced Learning) in Nursing  Education.
authors: Van Hoof, Thomas J | Leary, Catherine M | Banfi, Valori | Polifroni, E Carol
access_status: abstract and bibliographic record; full text not openly retrieved
corpus_or_sample: 25 research studies; all but one at prelicensure level
comparison: not consistently specified across mapped studies
outcomes: objective and subjective educational outcomes; terminology and reporting practices
principal_findings: Research was predominantly quantitative, but terminology and reporting were inconsistent and many intervention characteristics were undocumented.
key_limitations: Scoping review does not estimate effectiveness; full included-study table and detailed reporting fields were unavailable in the accessible abstract.
next_action: Request full text because the intervention-characteristic map is directly relevant to ARA instrumentation.

title: Anki Use and Academic Performance in Medical Education: A Systematic Review of  Evidence and Learning Theory.
authors: Frappa, Nicholas | Chernov, Danil | Dillon, Morgan | Alben, Matthew G
mechanism_or_intervention: Anki use integrating flashcards, retrieval practice and spaced repetition
comparison: nonusers, minimal users, frequency groups or structured interventions across studies
outcomes: USMLE Step 1/Step 2 CK and university examinations
principal_findings: Regular or high-frequency Anki use was positively associated with some Step 1 outcomes, while course-exam findings were mixed and the single Step 2 CK study was null.
quantitative_summary: Three studies showed consistent Step 1 associations; high-frequency users exceeded minimal users by 4–13 points in some studies.
key_limitations: Evidence largely observational; inconsistent definitions of Anki use, deck quality, preparation duration and outcome measures; self-selection and study-habit confounding.
next_action: Retain as central product review; do not treat association as causal effectiveness.

title: The Effectiveness of Spaced Learning, Interleaving, and Retrieval Practice in  Radiology Education: A Systematic Review.
authors: Thompson, Cole P | Hughes, Marion A
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
access_status: open full text under publisher licence
corpus_or_sample: 8 randomized or quasi-randomized studies from 1,316 records
mechanism_or_intervention: spaced learning, interleaving and retrieval practice
outcomes: immediate and delayed post-intervention examination scores
principal_findings: Five of eight studies reported significant differences favoring an intervention on at least one immediate or delayed assessment, but the domain evidence base was small.
quantitative_summary: 2 spacing studies, 2 interleaving studies, 6 retrieval studies; 2 studies combined spacing and retrieval.
key_limitations: Only eight eligible trials; single-reviewer data extraction; varied interventions and assessment timing; significance counts rather than pooled effect.
next_action: Retain as domain-specific synthesis and map its eight trials against broader health-professions reviews.

title: The Effectiveness of Spaced Repetition in Medical Education: A Systematic Review  and Meta-Analysis.
corpus_or_sample: 14 studies in review; 13 in meta-analysis; 21,415 learners
mechanism_or_intervention: spaced repetition delivered through flashcards, emailed MCQs, CME frameworks or classroom quizzes
principal_findings: The pooled result favored spaced repetition, but the intervention category combined materially different delivery systems.
key_limitations: Clinical and educational heterogeneity; mixed intervention forms; limited long-term and continuing-education evidence; optimal schedule and delivery remain unresolved.
product_or_mechanism: mechanism family containing products and course interventions
next_action: Retain as central quantitative synthesis; inspect primary-study overlap before combining with Trumble or Frappa.

title: Transfer of test-enhanced learning: Meta-analytic review and synthesis.
authors: Pan, Steven C | Rickard, Timothy C
access_status: detailed abstract and author manuscript located
domain_population: laboratory and educational transfer studies over more than 40 years
outcomes: transfer to changed formats, application, inference, diagnosis and new cues
principal_findings: Retrieval practice produced a moderate average transfer benefit, but positive transfer depended strongly on response congruency, elaborated retrieval and initial success.
quantitative_summary: d=0.40, 95% CI 0.31–0.50; bias adjustments substantially reduced intercept estimates when favorable moderators were absent.
key_limitations: Highly heterogeneous transfer categories; publication-bias models weakened unconditional estimates; laboratory evidence dominates several categories.
next_action: Retain as central transfer synthesis; avoid interpreting d=0.40 as universal transfer.

title: A Systematic Review of Quizlet in Vocabulary Acquisition
corpus_or_sample: 25 journal studies from ERIC and Web of Science, described as published in the prior four years
mechanism_or_intervention: Quizlet as a supplementary vocabulary-learning tool
comparison: varied designs and comparators across included studies
outcomes: vocabulary expansion, retention, motivation, engagement and attitudes
principal_findings: The review reports mostly positive vocabulary and affective findings across the included studies.
key_limitations: Narrow database/time window; descriptive synthesis; likely substantial overlap with the 2024 Quizlet meta-analysis; positive conclusions combine learning and affective outcomes.
next_action: Retain but create primary-study overlap map against Özdemir and Seçkin before synthesis.

title: Retrieval Practice Consistently Benefits Student Learning: A Systematic Review of Applied Research in Schools and Classrooms
authors: Agarwal, Pooja K. | Nunes, Ludmila D. | Blunt, Janell R.
access_status: open accepted manuscript and publisher metadata
domain_population: schools and classrooms across education levels/content areas
mechanism_or_intervention: retrieval practice in authentic educational settings
comparison: restudy, no retrieval or other classroom conditions
outcomes: student learning on delayed/immediate classroom assessments
principal_findings: Retrieval practice was beneficial across many settings and formats; 57% of effects were medium or large.
quantitative_summary: 49 effects; 57% medium/large; only 6% of experiments in non-WEIRD countries.
key_limitations: Not a pooled meta-analytic mean; applied studies varied; geographic concentration substantially limits transfer to Brazil/Portugal and other contexts.
next_action: Retain as central applied review and geographic-gap evidence.

title: A Meta-Analytic Review of the Effectiveness of Spacing and Retrieval Practice for Mathematics Learning
authors: Ewan Murray | Aidan J. Horner | Silke M. Göbel
domain_population: mathematics learning in isolated and course-embedded settings
corpus_or_sample: spacing: 27 studies/53 effects; testing vs restudy: 7 studies/32 effects
principal_findings: Spacing showed a robust small-to-medium benefit; the smaller retrieval-practice evidence base did not show a robust overall effect.
quantitative_summary: Spacing g=0.28 overall; isolated g=0.43; course-embedded g=0.24. Testing vs restudy g=0.18 with 95% CI crossing zero.
key_limitations: Few retrieval studies; smaller effects than other domains; isolated-learning effects were larger but less robust; mathematics tasks and courses varied.
next_action: Retain as a major domain-specific counterweight to universal retrieval claims.

title: Learning Techniques to Improve Memory in Children: A Systematic Review
authors: Sara Cadavid | María Camila Cortés-Albornoz | Ana-María Gómez-Carvajal | Santiago David Mendoza-Ayús | Karlos Luna | María Daniela Olaya Galindo | Alberto Vélez-Van-Meerbeke | Claudia Talero-Gutiérrez
journal: European Journal of Psychology of Education
corpus_or_sample: 75 experimental papers; testing effect represented by 23 studies/44 experiments
comparison: massed study, restudy or alternative encoding conditions depending on technique
principal_findings: The reviewed techniques generally benefited memory across ages, but educationally authentic materials were uncommon except in testing-effect research.
quantitative_summary: 75 papers; 23 testing-effect studies with 44 experiments; qualitative systematic synthesis.
key_limitations: Many laboratory tasks and episodic-memory outcomes; limited curriculum materials and school implementation; multiple techniques were grouped in one review.
next_action: Retain as developmental evidence and as support for testing ecological validity in schools.
